paragraphs.source_en: At this time the Tōdō and Kyōgoku forces stationed at Shibai also launched attacks against Ōtani Yoshitsugu, Kinoshita Yoritsugu, and their men. But unlike Fukushima Masanori, Tōdō Takatora did not plunge into close combat at the outset. While ordering his men to assail the enemy with arrows and gunfire, he repeatedly sent secret envoys to the contingents of Wakisaka, Kutsuki, Ogawa, and Akaza, stationed below Mount Matsuo and to the left of the Nakasendō. Needless to say, their purpose was to persuade those men to change sides.

units.source_zh: 一个饿极了的人，面前摆满山珍海味，却不允许吃上一口，心中之焦急不难想象。

units.source_en: That was precisely how Ekei felt that morning.
units.source_zh: 今晨惠琼正有这种心绪。

paragraphs.source_zh: 惠琼陷入了苦闷。一个饿极了的人，面前摆满山珍海味，却不允许吃上一口，心中之焦急不难想象。今晨惠琼正有这种心绪。

paragraphs.source_en: In fact, it was Ekei who had arranged for the Mōri to take up position on Mount Nangū. He firmly believed that even if Mōri Terumoto did not take the field in person, it would still be the Mōri house that decided the outcome of this war. He had simply never expected Ieyasu to advance westward; and even after Ieyasu came, it had never occurred to him that he himself might suffer a crushing defeat.

units.source_en: In fact, it was Ekei who had arranged for the Mōri to take up position on Mount Nangū.

paragraphs.source_en: Eloquence was Ekei's greatest gift. Pressed again and again by Ekei, Hidemoto ran out of arguments and had no choice but to promise that he would advance: “I was wrong. I shall march at once and attack the enemy from the rear.”

paragraphs.source_en: It would be no exaggeration to say that Ekei delighted in displaying the power of his tongue. His judgment and calculations, his devotion to the Mōri house, and his goodwill toward the Toyotomi house were all beyond reproach. But under the fierce assault of Ikeda and Asano, all his tireless efforts came to nothing.

units.source_en: It would be no exaggeration to say that Ekei delighted in displaying the power of his tongue.

units.source_en: But under the fierce assault of Ikeda and Asano, all his tireless efforts came to nothing.

paragraphs.source_en: At the sound of gunfire, Ekei rose from his camp stool with a bloodless face. The only thing he could do was hurry in panic toward Natsuka Masaie's position.

paragraphs.source_zh: 听到枪声，惠琼面无血色地从床几上站起身，他唯一能做的，便是慌慌张张奔向长束正家阵地。

paragraphs.source_en: He had never thought very highly of Natsuka Masaie. Masaie had altered the ancient unit of land measurement known as the tan from three hundred and sixty tsubo to three hundred tsubo, thereby making the numerical extent of Japan's territory appear considerably larger, but this was no more than a petty clever trick. As a warrior, he was at best a man of the second or third rank.

paragraphs.source_en: Ekei rushed to Natsuka Masaie and implored him to persuade Hidemoto to descend the mountain. Ekei's urgency was Masaie's peril as well, so Masaie agreed at once and immediately sent his retainer Konishi Jizaemon up the mountain.

paragraphs.source_zh: 惠琼奔到长束正家处，恳求正家去劝说秀元下山。惠琼之急，便是正家之危，故正家一口答应，立刻派家臣小西治左卫门上山。

paragraphs.source_en: Yet Hidemoto still made no move. He had not deceived Ekei. In fact, immediately after making his promise, he had declared to Kikkawa his intention to descend the mountain, only to be flatly refused.

paragraphs.source_en: In truth, there was no possibility that they would take action. Without Hidemoto's knowledge, Kikkawa Hiroie had already consulted Fukuhara Hirotoshi, Shishido Narimune, and other senior Mōri retainers. The previous night he had written to the four generals Ii Naomasa, Honda Tadakatsu, Fukushima Masanori, and Kuroda Nagamasa to seek peace, and had even sent them a sworn pledge.

paragraphs.source_en: At that very moment, the sworn pledge was probably in Ii Naomasa's hands. paragraphs.source_en: This was likely the secret stratagem that Kikkawa Hiroie, who had regarded Ieyasu favorably from the beginning, had devised after much anxious thought for the sake of the Mōri house. paragraphs.source_en: The enemy drew closer step by step, while a storm of gunfire swept across their positions. Ekei was not alone; Natsuka Masaie and Chōsokabe Morichika faced the same predicament. At first the attackers had exercised some caution, watching for movement on the mountain even as they advanced. Now they paid it no heed at all and hurled themselves into the assault with all their might.

paragraphs.source_en: Blood stained the withered grass red, and frenzied slaughter filled the battlefield. Among these men who understood self-restraint in ordinary life, were there any besides the Mōri and Kobayakawa Hideaki who still retained their reason? Of course there were. One was Shimazu Yoshihiro, seated in silent meditation within his lines; the other was Konishi Yukinaga.
